chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, all said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Go to the standing place of Jibraeel (peace be upon him), and it is beneath the water spout, for it was his standing place when he sought permission to visit the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And say: O Benevolent! O Generous! O Near! O Remote! I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family, and I ask You to return Your bounties to me.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And that is a place wherein a menstruating woman, facing the Qiblah, would not supplicate with the supplication of the blood, except that she would see purity, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.دُعَاءِ الدَّمِ: The supplication of the blood (recited by menstruating women)
key_terms.مَقَامَ جَبْرَئِيلَ: The standing place of the Angel Jibraeel

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the standing place of Jibraeel and the supplication recited there for ritual purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual significance of the Miqam Jibraeel, located beneath the mosque's water spout, as a locus for divine acceptance of supplication. It prescribes invoking God with attributes of generosity and nearness, while also noting a specific ritual benefit for menstruating women who recite the supplication facing the Qiblah, linking physical purity with spiritual devotion. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of prophetic traditions and the sanctity of specific spaces within the Masjid al-Nabi.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, altogether said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go to the standing place of Jibraeel<sup>as</sup>, and it is beneath the water sprout, and it was his<sup>as</sup> standing place when he<sup>as</sup> sought permission to (visit) Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and say, ‘O Benevolent! O Generous! O Near! O Remote! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> to Send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the People<sup>asws</sup> of his<sup>saww</sup> Household; and I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> to Return upon me Your<sup>azwj</sup> Bounties’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And that is a place wherein a menstruating woman would not supplicate facing the Qiblah, the supplication of the blood, except that she would see purity, if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Am mar all of them have said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You should go to the Station of Jibril, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and it is under al-Mizab. This place was his station wherefrom he asked permission from the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. You should say at this place, ‘O generous, O Honorable, O the one who is very near, O the one who is far. I appeal before You to grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause). I appeal before You to return to me Your bounty.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘This is a station where if a women experiencing menses, facing the direction of al-Ka‘bah, prays with the prayer for experiencing menses, she will see herself clean, if Allah so wills.’”
